problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(0,1,2)$, $B(-1,0,1)$, $C(1,1,0)$, and $D(3,-1,3).$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Volume of a Parallelepiped Spanned by Three Position Vectors Given Their Coordinates
examples.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(3,-1,2),$ $B(2,1,1),$ $C(-1,2,1),$ and $D(4,4,2).$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-i+2j-k \\  & =⟨-1,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+2j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-4i+3j-k \\  & =⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+4j+2k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =i+5j \\  & =⟨1,5,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3\cdot 0-5\cdot (-1))-2((-4)\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1))-((-4)\cdot 5-1\cdot 3) \\  & =-5-2+23 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

$$
V=|16|=16.
$$

feedback.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,2,2⟩$, $b=⟨3,0,2⟩$ and $c=⟨4,1,3⟩$ are coplanar.
feedback.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 3-1\cdot 2)-2(3\cdot 3-4\cdot 2)+2(3\cdot 1-4\cdot 0) \\  & =-2k-2+6 \\  & =-2k+4.\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ -2k+4 & =0 \\ 2k & =4 \\ k & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=2.$
